statement.p: Calculate all four second-order partial derivatives and check that f_{xy}=f_{yx}. Assume the variables are restricted to a domain on which the function is defined. f(x,y) = 5\sin\mathopen{}\left(2x\right)\cos\mathopen{}\left(6y\right)

static.solution: f_x = 10\cos\mathopen{}\left(2x\right)\cos\mathopen{}\left(6y\right) and f_y = -30\sin\mathopen{}\left(2x\right)\sin\mathopen{}\left(6y\right), so f_{xx} = -20\sin\mathopen{}\left(2x\right)\cos\mathopen{}\left(6y\right), f_{yy} = -180\sin\mathopen{}\left(2x\right)\cos\mathopen{}\left(6y\right), and f_{xy} = -60\cos\mathopen{}\left(2x\right)\sin\mathopen{}\left(6y\right) = f_{yx} = -60\cos\mathopen{}\left(2x\right)\sin\mathopen{}\left(6y\right).
